Ioctl dispatch, permission checks, and get versus set state machines.
Validation ranges for flow types, hash functions, tunable IDs, and FEC combinations.
Kernel entry points and driver callback contracts beyond these header layouts.
Byte order, packing, and 32 versus 64 bit compatibility handling.

findings.text: Two small helpers extract subfields from a 64-bit ring cookie: one keeps the low queue or ring selector and one isolates the virtual-function selector then shifts it down. Both take the cookie by value and return the selected portion.
Ring cookie layout reserves the low 32 bits for ring selection, the next 8 bits for VF selection, and a shift of 32 to recover the VF value.

Receive network flow classifier request carries a command word, flow type, opaque data word, embedded flow specification, a shared slot usable either as rule count or RSS context, and a trailing variable length list of rule locations.

Receive hash indirection table carries command plus entry count and trailing ring indices. The fuller hash object carries command, RSS context, table and key sizes, hash function and transform selectors with reserved bytes, a reserved word, and trailing configuration words.
RSS context allocation request and no-change indirection marker both use the all-bits-set 32-bit sentinel value.

Legacy n-tuple flow entry holds a flow type, paired header and mask unions covering several IPv4 transport shapes plus Ethernet header or raw bytes, VLAN tag and mask, data and mask words, and a signed action field. The surrounding n-tuple wrapper holds only a command and one such entry.
N-tuple actions use negative sentinels for drop and for clearing a filter. Flash file names are bounded at 128 bytes and the flash operation enumeration defines an all-regions zero value.

Flash request holds command, region selector, and fixed filename buffer. Dump object holds command, version, flag, length, and trailing payload. Feature query block holds four state words and its container holds command, block count, and trailing blocks. Feature set block holds valid and requested words with an analogous container.
Firmware dump disable is zero.
Timestamping capability object reports command, socket timestamping flags, PHC index, transmit type mask with three reserved words, and receive filter mask with three reserved words.
Feature negotiation result uses three low bit positions for unsupported, wish, and compat indications. The per-queue queue universe is capped at 4096 entries.

Per-queue operation holds command, subcommand, a bitmask sized to cover the maximum queue count in 32-bit units, and trailing data. Forward error correction parameters hold command, active mode mask, requested mode mask, and a reserved word.
FEC configuration defines six ordered bit positions for none, auto, off, RS, base-R, and low-latency RS modes, each exposed as a single-bit mask.

Traditional ethtool command numbers start at 1 for deprecated get settings and 2 for deprecated set settings, then assign successive small values through link query, EEPROM, coalescing, ring, pause, checksum, scatter gather, self test, strings, identify, stats, TSO, permanent address, UFO, GSO, flags, and private flags operations.

Later ethtool commands continue the dense numeric sequence from the receive-hash and GRO region through receive classification, flashing, reset, n-tuple, string-set info, features, channels, dump, timestamp, module, EEE, SSH hash, tunables, PHY stats, per-queue, link settings, PHY tunables, and FEC get and set operations. SPARC aliases repeat the deprecated settings pair.

Link mode advertisement uses a dense zero-based bit index space beginning with legacy 10 through 1000 megabit modes, autonegotiation, port types, pause, backplane and higher-rate optics, then extending past bit 31 to cover 25G and above plus FEC reporting and newer single-pair and very-high-rate modes. A terminal count enumerator ends the list.
Only indices up to 31 may use the legacy single-word mask form; higher indices require the newer link-settings interface. The legacy helper maps a mode name to one shifted bit in an unsigned long.

Supported capability macros for the legacy modes each expand to the legacy helper applied to the corresponding link mode name, covering the same low-index modes from 10 megabit through 56G backplane variants.

Several objects use trailing flexible members whose length is governed by a separate size or count field supplied in the same request, including rule locations, indirection entries, RSS words, dump payload, feature blocks, and per-queue data.

Callers must size buffers using the accompanying count fields and the fixed filename and queue-mask bounds; mismatched counts can truncate rule lists, hash tables, feature blocks, dump data, or per-queue payloads.
